correctness.rationale: The explicitly stated IID coupon model and exact final-draw multinomial coefficient law were reconstructed. Log-concave coefficient sequences remain log-concave under convolution, so the Toeplitz kernel has nonnegative ordered minors. At each admissible integer time, the Cauchy–Binet minor contains the strictly positive boundary summand a_h^2(c_r b_s-c_s b_r) for indices r=n-h and s=r+1, including m=2 and p0=0. Normalization yields strict reverse MLR. Earliest-time uniformity, the next-step profile, independence iff equal rates, negative monotone-transform covariance under finite moments and asymptotic rarest-label uniformity follow by direct algebra and exponential-rate comparison. The stand-alone exact-rational dynamic program passes 5416 assertions; finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The identified nonuniform quota-completion coefficient formula is classical (May, 2008) and not claimed as original. The new claim is a strict pairwise likelihood-ratio ordering of terminal coupon labels conditional on every exact completion time, valid for every positive required probability vector, every common quota, and optional null mass. Primary sources examined did not make this implication; generic total positivity is a proof method, not a published coupon-specific statement. Unresolved historical-priority risks are disclosed.
residual_risks: May gives the essential terminal-label coefficient formula; an unlocated previous TP2 analysis could imply or state the exact conditional ordering.
Older general log-concavity and coupon-collector dependence literature is not exhaustively catalogued; independent historical priority review remains desirable.
The relevant Mahmoud–Smythe full text is now accessible and inspected, but other older general dependence results may be unlocated.

value.rationale: The coupon collector naturally asks which rare type ultimately controls collection. The theorem identifies a universal nonasymptotic conditional likelihood-ratio ordering over every completion time and every positive heterogeneous required type probability, all equal integer quotas, and null mass. This is structurally stronger than scalar moments, exposes an if-and-only-if independence boundary, and explains the late-time rarest-type asymptotic; it is not the known count formula or a one-off parameter substitution.
